One-Week Vegetarian Meal Plan

Seven days of satisfying meals, plus three recipes to cook and share.

Weekly meal plan

Meals include eggs and dairy. Choose cheeses made with microbial or other vegetarian rennet. Adjust portions and snacks to suit your needs.

Each recipe below makes four servings; the plan uses one serving for dinner and one for lunch the next day. Refrigerate remaining portions promptly in shallow containers and use within 3–4 days or freeze. Reheat thoroughly; refrigerate cooked rice promptly.

1. Chickpea quinoa bowls

Serves: 4  |  Prep: 15 minutes  |  Cook: 25 minutes

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (170 g) dry quinoa, rinsed
  • 2 cups (480 ml) water
  • 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 2 bell peppers, diced
  • 1 medium cucumber, diced
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 2 tablespoons lemon juice
  • 4 oz (115 g) vegetarian feta, crumbled
  • ¼ cup chopped parsley; salt and pepper to taste

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Combine quinoa and water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff.
  2. Toss chickpeas and peppers with olive oil, cumin, paprika and a pinch each of salt and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring once.
  3. Divide the quinoa among four bowls. Top with the roasted mixture and cucumber.
  4. Drizzle with lemon juice and finish with feta and parsley. Season to taste.

Nutrition facts

Approximate per serving; ¼ of recipe.

Calories520 kcal
Protein20 g
Carbohydrates69 g
Fat19 g
Fiber13 g
Sodium560 mg

Cooking tip: Pat the chickpeas dry before roasting for better browning. Keep cucumber and feta separate from warm components when packing leftovers.

2. Lentil tomato pasta

Serves: 4  |  Prep: 10 minutes  |  Cook: 25 minutes

Ingredients

  • 12 oz (340 g) dry whole-wheat pasta
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 medium onion, finely diced
  • 1 medium carrot, grated
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1 can (28 oz / 795 g) crushed tomatoes
  • 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) lentils, drained and rinsed
  • 2 cups (60 g) baby spinach
  • ¼ cup (25 g) grated vegetarian hard cheese
  • Salt and black pepper to taste

Method

  1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the pasta according to package directions; reserve ½ cup cooking water, then drain.
  2. Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and carrot for 5–7 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add garlic and oregano and cook for 30 seconds.
  3. Stir in tomatoes and lentils. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add spinach and stir until wilted.
  4. Toss pasta with the sauce, adding a little reserved pasta water as needed. Season to taste and divide among four plates; sprinkle with cheese.

Nutrition facts

Approximate per serving; ¼ of recipe.

Calories520 kcal
Protein24 g
Carbohydrates91 g
Fat9 g
Fiber17 g
Sodium520 mg

Cooking tip: Save pasta water before draining: its starch helps the sauce cling. For a looser reheated sauce, add a splash of water.

3. Tofu vegetable curry with brown rice

Serves: 4  |  Prep: 15 minutes  |  Cook: 40 minutes

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (190 g) dry brown rice
  • 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, drained and cubed
  • 1 tablespoon neutral oil
  • 1 medium onion, sliced
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
  • 2 tablespoons curry powder
  • 1 can (13.5 oz / 400 ml) light coconut milk
  • ½ cup (120 ml) water
  • 1 bell pepper, sliced
  • 2 cups (about 180 g) broccoli florets
  • 1 cup (150 g) frozen peas
  • 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice

Method

  1. Cook the brown rice according to package directions, typically 35–45 minutes.
  2. Pat tofu dry. Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown tofu for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally; transfer to a plate.
  3. Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook for 3–4 minutes. Stir in garlic, ginger and curry powder; cook for 30 seconds.
  4. Add coconut milk, water, bell pepper and broccoli. Simmer for 8–10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
  5. Return tofu to the pan and add peas and soy sauce. Simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in lime juice. Serve over the rice.

Nutrition facts

Approximate per serving; ¼ of recipe, including rice.

Calories490 kcal
Protein19 g
Carbohydrates61 g
Fat20 g
Fiber7 g
Sodium250 mg

Cooking tip: Blot the tofu well so it browns rather than steams. Curry powders vary in heat; start with less if yours is spicy.

Nutrition values throughout are estimates based on typical ingredients, before optional added salt. Actual values vary with brands, preparation and portion sizes.
